Below is a practical, “no‑code‑or‑phased‑developers” guide to create a very simple **Admin Orders page** that only you (the site owner) can see. --- ## 1. Prepare Supabase ### 1.1 Create a “site‑owner” role 1. **Log in to Supabase** → **Database > Permissions** 2. Click **functions → Users**. 3. In the role list, create a new role called `site_owner`. 4. Grant **SELECT** on the `orders` table (and any related tables you want to inspect) to this role. > **Tip:** If you prefer to just use your own email, skip the role – you’ll simply check the email later. ### 1.2 Create an “admin” endpoint (optional, but safer) If you want to hide the data from other API requests, create a Supabase Edge Function: ``` supabase functions create adminOrders // Replace file contents with: export default async function handler(req, res) { const { data, error } = await supabase .from('orders') .select('*') .eq('created_by', req.parsedJwt.email) // or omit to fetch all if (error) return res.status(403).json({error}); res.json(data); } ``` > This way the data isn’t exposed until you authenticate. --- ## 2. Set Up Front‑End (e.g., React or Next.js) ### 2.1 Install Supabase client ```bash npm i @supabase/supabase-js ``` ### 2.2 Initialize Supabase in your app ```js // supabaseClient.js import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js' const supabaseUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL const supabaseAnonKey = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY export const supabase = createClient(supabaseUrl, supabaseAnonKey) ``` ### 2.3 Create the Admin page **File:** `pages/admin/orders.js` (Next.js) or `src/AdminOrders.jsx` (React) ```js import { useEffect, useState } from 'react' import { supabase } from '../supabaseClient' export default function AdminOrders() { const [orders, setOrders] = useState([]) const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true) const [error, setError] = useState(null) useEffect(() => { // 1️⃣ Get the current user const { data: { user } } = supabase.auth // 2️⃣ Allow only you (check email or role) const allowedEmail = 'your-email@example.com' // ← change to yours if (!user || user.email !== allowedEmail) { setError('Access denied') setLoading(false) return } // 3️⃣ Fetch all orders – only your role can run this const fetchOrders = async () => { const { data, error } = await supabase .from('orders') .select('*') // change to specific fields if you want .order('created_at', { ascending: false }) if (error) setError(error.message) else setOrders(data) setLoading(false) } fetchOrders() }, []) if (loading) return

Deploy / Test 1. **Build** your app (`npm run build`, `next build` etc.). 2. **Deploy** to Vercel, Netlify, or your hosting of choice. 3. **Log in** as yourself → navigate to `/admin/orders`. You should see the table; any other user will see “Access denied” (or be redirected). --- ## 4. Optional Enhancements | Feature | How | |---------|-----| | **Pagination** | Use `.range()` in Supabase query. | | **Search / Filters** | Add input fields and filter query (`.ilike('customer_name', `%${q}%`)`). | | **Role‑based auth** | Create a Supabase “role” called `site_owner` and check `supabase.auth.getUser().roles.includes('site_owner')`. | | **Secure function** | If you used the Edge Function, call it instead of `supabase.from('orders')`. | --- ### Final Checklist - [ ] Created `site_owner` role or set email guard. - [ ] Granted SELECT on `orders` to that role. - [ ] Added AdminOrders page with auth guard. - [ ] Tested with your account. - [ ] Deployed. You now have a one‑page admin dashboard that only you can access, displaying every customer’s order data on your Supabase‑backed app. Happy managing!
